3d-trigonometry:
What the notes actually say

Only two starred pointers, no worked example:

★ Use a model to explain how to identify right angled triangle! ★ Identify the angle between line and plane

Corroborating evidence from the printed worksheet

The worksheet under the notes is headed "III. Angle between line and plane." and carries:

  • Q15 — "In the rectangular box shown, find (a) AC (b) AR (c) angle BRC."
  • Q16 — "The diagram shows a cuboid of length 10 cm, with a square cross-section of side 5 cm. Calculate (a) the length AR, (b) angle RAC, (c) angle between RC and base ABCD, (d) the angle b…" (part (d) is cut off)

So the topic is taught on cuboids, asking first for a diagonal length, then for an angle.

⚠ The worksheet is background material visible in the photos, not part of the notes. It is recorded because it is directly readable evidence of the question format.

Method fingerprint

  • Use a model to identify the right-angled triangle inside the solid.
  • Identify the angle between a line and a plane.
  • The notes give two pointers and no worked example — this topic is the least developed of the eight.

Two letters matter. Scenario 2 uses nnn and kkk because the two odd numbers are independent; using nnn twice would only prove it for the same number. The notes make this change silently — no note explains it.

Corrections the notes make to themselves. "positive" is caret-inserted in Scenario 1 and "odd" in Scenario 2. Both are corrections to the precision of the statement, not the algebra — the notes treat stating the claim exactly as part of the proof.

Method fingerprint

  • Fixed opening: 'Let 2 consecutive odd numbers be 2n+1 and 2n+3'.
  • Odd as 2n+1, never 2n−1; consecutive odds by +2, not a second letter.
  • Two independent odd numbers use two letters: 2n+1 and 2k+1.
  • Proof terminates by reaching a form — 2(…), 2(…)+1, 8(…) — with no concluding sentence.
  • Precision corrections inserted by caret: 'positive', 'odd'.
  • Place-value: two-digit number as 10x+y, reverse 10y+x, kept in place-value form, then the 'borrow 10' regrouping.

bearings:
The notes' one instruction: how to sketch

The sketch on shows the convention the notes want reproduced:

  • point AAA circled, with a North arrow drawn at AAA — the point you measure from;
  • CCC up-left, AC=8 kmAC = 8\text{ km}AC=8 km, angle from N to ACACAC marked 19∘19^\circ19∘;
  • BBB up-right, AB=11 kmAB = 11\text{ km}AB=11 km, angle from N to ABABAB marked 41∘41^\circ41∘;
  • a long arc sweeping round AAA labelled 341∘341^\circ341∘.

341∘341^\circ341∘ is the bearing of CCC from AAA: measured clockwise from north, the full way round rather than 19∘19^\circ19∘ anticlockwise. The notes write only the number — the relationship 341=360−19341 = 360 - 19341=360−19 is not written on the sheet.

The bearing of BBB from AAA is 041∘041^\circ041∘ — three figures, leading zero.

The notes do not carry this into a sine/cosine rule calculation, although the two distances and the included angle 19∘+41∘=60∘19^\circ+41^\circ = 60^\circ19∘+41∘=60∘ would allow one.

Method fingerprint

  • The starred instruction is 'how to sketch!' — the sketch is the skill.
  • North line drawn at the point being measured from.
  • Three-figure bearings including reflex values — 341° is shown with an anticlockwise arc.
  • Two legs from one point with distances and angles from north (8 km / 19°, 11 km / 41°).

16x−1=64x16^{x-1}=6^{4x}16x−1=64x looks like a log question, but the notes reduce it first:

24x−4=24x×34x  ⇒  2−4=34x2^{4x-4}=2^{4x}\times 3^{4x} \;\Rightarrow\; 2^{-4}=3^{4x}24x−4=24x×34x⇒2−4=34x

Only now are logs applied, giving x=−log⁡2log⁡3x=-\dfrac{\log 2}{\log 3}x=−log3log2​.
